Brief rewritten 2026-08-07 — the original approach was wrong for this tree. 🔴 Do not file-copy the DB: (a) task 41's Phase 1 established there is no way to write a file from JS here — no RNFS, no FS TurboModule, op-sqlite gives paths but no write; and (b) a byte-copy of a live SQLite DB is unsafe anyway — with an open WAL it can capture a torn state, which would have been a latent integrity bug even with a filesystem API. What exists is better: op-sqlite's DB object has execute, delete(), attach/detach, getDbPath, loadFile, so the whole ladder is reachable at SQL level with no new native module — VACUUM INTO for an atomic consistent backup, PRAGMA integrity_check, ATTACH + INSERT…SELECT for salvage (which also answers what salvage reads — it skips views and steps past a corrupt table). ✅ VACUUM INTO availability RESOLVED headlessly 2026-08-17 — it is a build fact, not a device fact. The brief said to verify it on device and stop if absent. op-sqlite 17.1.2 compiles its own bundled amalgamation (cpp/sqlite3.c, wired at android/CMakeLists.txt:79) at SQLite 3.51.3, with no SQLITE_OMIT_VACUUM/SQLITE_OMIT_ATTACH flags — it does not link Android system SQLite, so the version does not vary by device or OS. 3.51.3 ≫ the 3.27 floor. Phase A can build on it with confidence; Phase B still watches it run, as habit rather than doubt. 🔴 One gap: nothing reports free disk space — attempt-and-catch SQLITE_FULL, setReservedBytes, or a small native call; bring the tradeoff back, since "block before starting" implies knowing in advance. ⚠ backup_log (migration 001) has never been written to or read — 14 is its only natural consumer; use it or retire it. Ruled 2026-08-07: logging will be pruned/dropped as we move from closed beta to open beta to general release. The mechanism, not a mood: the closed-beta safeguard is human review of a small volume from known people — and that does not scale, and fails silently. The stream must narrow exactly where the protection stops being real. Open beta: free-text conversation capture is dropped; structured streams (performance, outcomes, timings, model-I/O metadata, thermal, errors) survive, because they carry 17/19/20's signal with almost none of the exposure. GA: minimal or nothing. Prune by dropping, not disabling. Anonymization is best-effort on free text and "anonymized" never means "safe to publish" — the real risk is re-identification by combination, since a task list is close to a fingerprint even fully scrubbed. That asymmetry (structured anonymizes completely, free text doesn't) is what makes the ladder principled rather than an arbitrary line. ⚠ See the corpus-window consequence in the frontier section. Where the frontier is — two threads, and they don't compete

🔴 The corpus collection window is finite, and that reprices everything below. The capture ladder (43) drops free-text conversation capture at open beta — permanently ending the supply of real conversational input that 31's corpus, 38's training data and 40's held-out eval all depend on. The corpus is built during alpha and closed beta, or it is largely not built at all, and every future LoRA iteration and every re-run of the bake-off draws on a corpus whose window has already shut. This is an argument for starting 41 now rather than after the beta-hardening work, and for closed beta being generous with free-text capture while consent and review are still real protections. It is not an argument for extending the window — the mechanism in 43 doesn't bend.

Thread 1 — the strategic one (the model-migration decision). Now 41 → 31 → 38 → 40, then Jason's call. Task 41 is the new front of the chain and it's the move that can happen today: once capture is on, the corpus accumulates while you do everything else, which is the only input on the board that grows without effort. 31's interview and reconstruction work runs in parallel with the capture window rather than waiting on it.

Thread 2 — the tree, then beta hardening. ✅ (a) the three checks on main — done 2026-08-17, green; ✅ (b) push main to GitHub — done; ✅ (c) task 37 — done. Landed since: 48, 14 Phase A, 41 (both phases), 44. Remaining: 15 / 17 / 21 / 32 and the designed visual pass.

Sequencing note — task 17 vs. the device session (2026-08-18). 17 is headless, Opus-worthy, and the natural owner of the completion_count/success_rate writer task 44 just left as a deliberate seam — so its context is freshest now. But the recommendation is the device session first, for three reasons: (1) four tasks' worth of code — 14, 41, 48, 44 — have never run on the S23 FE, and it is the biggest unverified surface on the board; running 17 first only piles more never-run code on an unverified base, and if the first build reveals a problem (a grammar that won't compile, migration 007 failing on real op-sqlite, the capture TurboModule not loading) everything above it is suspect. (2) Capture accumulating the corpus is the one time-limited resource — the window closes at open beta, and capture only starts collecting once it is on the phone; every day it is off the phone is corpus not gathered. (3) 17 learns from real usage data, so its value (not just its mechanism) is only real once device use has generated some. 17 is the right parallel work only if the device session cannot happen soon — it is exactly the headless set-and-forget batch to hand off when Jason is away from the phone, with the caveat that it builds on ground not yet verified.

Sequencing note added 2026-08-17 — 37 before 41, and it is nearly free. Task 37 is a small, headless, no-P grammar fix that is already spike-confirmed (first char [a-zA-Z0-9]; min-length does not work). Task 41 turns on capture, and every capture taken through the unfixed grammar is corpus recorded against a known-defective extractor. Since 41's whole purpose is to feed 31/38/40, landing 37 first costs a few hours and protects the entire corpus window; landing it after means some fraction of the irreplaceable alpha corpus carries a defect the board already knows about. The two do not compete for the same resource — 37 is headless, 41 needs the phone.
